Definition: a brick (from the whiteness of the clay)
BiblicalUsage: lᵉbênâh means a brick — an ordinary word that carries real weight in the Bible. In Exodus 1:14, "and in brick"; and in Exodus 5:7, "Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick". In Genesis 11:3, "let us make brick"; and in Isaiah 65:3, "and burneth incense upon altars of brick".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe bricks tell two stories — Babel's builders burned them to make a name for themselves, and Pharaoh's slaves made them until their lives were bitter. I hold that God judges both towers and taskmasters: no human work built on pride or cruelty stands. My position is that I will not build my name out of other people's suffering.
